utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before -- no, there are a few procedural issues I'll deal with later today but still today, that's the request by Mr. Emmerson for nonsitting days in July and there's also a matter of an appeals hearing which affects Mr. Guy-Smith. We'll deal with that, but first, Mr. Emmerson, I'd like you -- to give you the opportunity to continue your cross-examination. Mr. Pappas, before we continue, I'd like to remind you, as I did yesterday, that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I leave it to you. I think we -- yesterday we finished in open session. I think it was the Kaufmann book which did not ask for any private session. If that would be different, please inform the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, as soon as it's necessary to refer to any Rule 70 material, at that stage I will ask to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, I want to begin where I left off yesterday afternoon by asking you one or two further questions about the incident which occurred on the 11th of August. Now, we have -- we have a short summary from you in the evidence that you have given of the way that Mr. Haradinaj conducted himself during that meeting. I want, if I may, to put on the record with you and invite you to confirm the contents of your consolidated witness statement where you deal with this matter. So I'm just going to read the passages to you and ask you, please, to confirm that these are an accurate reflection of your evidence because they don't find their way into the written statement that has been admitted in evidence in this case. Quotation - and I'm reading from the second half of paragraph 24, the consolidated witness statement, and then on: "He was absolutely calm and controlled, and in a gentle way he started interrogating us one by one. He was polite. He started with Penti, who was obviously shocked, frightened from the development of things (Penti had been visiting our team for just that day and this had happened to him). He checked his papers and only had a short discussion with him. Now, I recall that he asked Penti a question about a lake in Finland that was the subject of some dispute with the Russians, and Penti answered him. After Penti, he asked the interpreter in Albanian a few things; however, I'm not aware about the content of their conversation. After Kastriot, he turned to me and asked me about my whereabouts and occupation back home. He told me that he has no problem with Greeks, although the politics of my country build-up hostile feelings in a lot of his comrades. He told me that he had visited Greece several times and that he has a lot of Albanian friends living there, and some of them came to Kosovo to fight with him. I explained to him the circumstances in which we had ended up there, meaning our presence in Rznic. I explained to him our mandate and the purpose of our presence in Kosovo. It seemed to me that he understood and was satisfied with my explanations. Afterwards he spoke in French and English with Kaufmann." And then a little further on, paragraph 26, I want to put the following passage on the record: "Afterwards the commander came with us to our car, and he started to search it thoroughly inside and outside. He asked us if we had guns, and we said no. After this he told us that we are free to go. He offered us an escort out of the area, which we agreed to. He then ordered the three men in the black uniform, including Idriz Balaj, who had stopped us before, to escort us out of Gllogjan." And then finally two lines at the bottom of paragraph 26: "The whole incident lasted for about one and a half hours under continuous shelling of Serbian artillery." So, first of all, can I ask you, please, to confirm that that is an reflection of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And secondly, just one or two supplementary questions. It follows from that description that your impression of Mr. Haradinaj was that he remained calm throughout this interchange and behaved reasonably to you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this was despite the fact that the village of Gllogjan and the village of Irzniq were under heavy fire, and the Serbs were closing in?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were under shelling, yes. I don't know, it's our estimation that the Serbs were very close, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you know from the video you saw yesterday, that by the following day they overrun Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, for a commander to come away from the front line, to divert himself and others from combat to deal with a group of monitors who had decided to drive straight into the heart of a front line zone, would you accept this is obviously a rather unwelcome distraction from the job of defending people's lives in the course of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the way that you put it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But nonetheless, once he had established your good faith, he not only returned your documents and ensured that you could leave but gave you safe passage out of the area, diverting soldiers again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I have to ask you to slow down for the interpreters. Could you perhaps, please, repeat your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I said: Nonetheless, once he had established your good faith, he not only returned your documents and ensured that you could leave but gave you safe passage out of the area, again diverting soldiers from the front line to meet the needs of providing you with protection?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, before I turn to the issues surrounding your visit to Hotel Pashtrik and the Lake Radoniq canal area in September, I just want to ask you one or two questions about an incident that you describe in your consolidated witness statement at paragraph 14. And if I can just remind you of it without asking you necessarily to turn it up. You say in your consolidated witness statement that there was an incident that you yourselves witnessed at the beginning of August in the countryside area to the east of the main Peje-Gjakove road and south of the Peje-Pristina road, where you said in your witness statement that there were strange utterly deserted villages. Do you remember that expression?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You described finding the body of an Albanian man lying next to a street at the entrance to the village, and you said that the body was decayed and had been mutilated by animals. And then you said this, and I quote from your statement: "The village itself was abandoned, and it seemed that the villagers as well as the KLA had retreated from there, although I should point out that this was an area where we did not see armed uniformed KLA soldiers with KLA insignia manning check-points. On the same day, I recall we drove down a small road towards a village also in the same area where the body was found, and suddenly we saw a Serb tank on the road with its gun-barrel pointed towards us. We approached slowly and were given permission to continue into the village, and in the village we saw Serb soldiers looting houses and burning them. Surprisingly, they did not seem anxious that we were there. This was the first and only time that I saw Serbian forces away from the main roads during my time in this posting." Can you help us as to, first of all, where this village was that you witnessed Serb forces looting and burning houses?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact -- the exact location, but I can say that it was on the main road, if we -- if we can take the main road as a point of reference from Pec to Pristina, almost 30 kilometres away from Pec and on the south. Very close to the road, we start to see abandoned villages, and further -- a little bit further, we started to see these images that I told you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, did you say on that road from Pec to Pristina almost 13 or 30 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 30. 30, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be obvious, but why did it surprise you that the Serb soldiers did not seem anxious that you were there?

As I stated before in other parts of my statement, when they wanted to hide something, they would refuse the team to pass from check-points. So we were very surprised to see that the men on the tank let us pass and go into the village, and the others were looting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So your experience was that if the Serbs refused you access to a particular area, that would generally lead you to believe that there was something there at that time that they were trying to hide from your view. Is that correct?
Yeah, that was the -- the feeling, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did that happen in relation to the canal? Was there a period of time when you were being denied access to the canal by the Serb police?
I'm not aware about that because the first time I heard about this canal was on 17th of September, where I was in district prosecutor office.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's what I want to try to explore with you, Mr. Pappas. You wrote a report to your own government, and on -- I think probably even although Rule 70 has not been claimed in respect to this --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, with respect, I think it is, and I understand from Mr. Pappas that this is -- I have no problem with Mr. Emmerson using it, of course, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's better done in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be just for this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think from this point onwards, in fact, for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then -- from this point on --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- for a while. Yes. Then we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, has this video already received an MFI number?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, it hasn't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Registrar, that would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be marked for identification as D66.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Do I understand that it's then the transcript that gets D66 and that the video is attached to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The video receives the number and everything that -- and all the text will be attached. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we play the video now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I could just -- just ask to pause it for one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, you identified yesterday a photograph which you say that you took of the Gllogjan KLA HQ with a pile of rubble outside it and which you told us was rubble that was not there when you visited the HQ on the 11th of August. As you'll see in just a moment, this is the same building. I think you can be in a position to confirm. I'm going to ask you to look for images of Judge Gojkovic arguing with Mr. Kaufmann and of yourself being present at the time, and I'll point out to you the individual who I'm going to suggest to you is yourself. If I'm wrong, obviously you'll tell me.
Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pausing there for a moment, if you would.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You recognise the Land Rover?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we can just pause again for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You recognise the building?
Yes, that's a building.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pause there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The gentleman in the suit is Judge Gojkovic, I suggest, and the gentleman in the hat is Mr. Kaufmann. Is that correct?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you clarify for us, please?
The man in the suit is, I believe, Cvejic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The other judge?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And the man in the hat?
Is Kaufmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic is the prosecutor's name. And this one is Judge Cvejic?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He is, in fact, I think, an investigating judge, Judge Gojkovic, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is the other gentleman -- just pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is the other gentleman that you met at the Peje --
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- port on the 17th for the first time?
Yes, along with Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "He said -- he said then -- then they want to open the cars because you can always have the problems if -- if you're not subjective or -- or something, because they are asking you from where you're in Kosovo and -- well, do you know where the headquarters was? You said no, and then you are coming to the headquarters. "Yes, I said we were -- I said we were somewhere. "Excuse me. Is this something which goes into TV?"

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pause there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that you walking behind there?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "No, just to prove you -- prove you that you have been here and ... "Everything -- everything is possible, but it's not fair and it's not correct to tell us that the police prevented him from going inside."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we can pause it there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check where the French translation -- what I wanted to know is whether you are at a point where we could continue in English. I -- from what I understood, you were translating the English text. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The English is not reading anything. The other booths are from the text --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... from the transcript. But, Mr. Di Fazio, I think, as a matter of fact, that from the transcript if we would like to know more about the text spoken originally, that we could try to find out that. It might not be the core of the issue at stake here, so therefore for the time being I would like to focus on what apparently the interpreter tells us in this video-clip, because we do not have a full translation of the originally spoken language. At least that's my impression but of course I can't -- .

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If I can assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: We're happy to proceed on the basis of this translation for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So is the Defence, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think -- this is a Prosecution translation. I think a distinction is drawn if one reads closely between what is translated from the original by the translation unit and what is simply a transcript of the words spoken by the English interpreter present. So, for example, on the page numbered 51, which is the second page of transcript, the first passage seems to be a translation by the translation unit of the words immediately before, whereas a few lines further down interpreter into English one has a transcription of the words spoken by the English-speaking interpreter on the film. I think that is a -- it may not resolve all possible wrinkles, but I think that is the way to read the document. It -- may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's not entirely clear to me, but for the time being, I think we can proceed on the basis of what we have. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can see from certain passages in this transcript, Mr. Pappas, that there is plainly a conversation taking place between the man you have identified as Judge Cvejic --
I'm sorry, can I have the passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Have you not been provided with a copy of the transcript?
Not only this, but what you say. I have to have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there is a problem with the -- no, I think the witness is not able to see the LiveNote on the screen. Is that the problem?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's see whether -- you would like to hear what Mr. Emmerson said or you would like to hear what was said during the video-clip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What Mr. Emmerson said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What Mr. Emmerson said. And in relation to what exactly because we could then -- or he could repeat it to you and we could read it --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the witness is concerned that his screen was showing a video rather than displaying the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He would like to follow the questions and answers in LiveNote. I think that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, we can't show you at the same time the video and the text spoken by Mr. Emmerson. If you would please assist Mr. Emmerson in identifying exactly what you would like he repeats so that you can at least listen carefully to what he says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I would like him to repeat what he starting saying after the video was played.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Well, I'll ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's apparent from the transcript that we have - and I don't know whether you have it available to you or not - but it's apparent, from the transcript that we have, that the conversation that's taking place between Mr. Kaufmann and Judge Cvejic as you have identified him as being is concerned with exclusion of your team by the police. So, for example, if you look at page 52 -- I'm sorry, I do apologise, page 54 at the bottom the speaker's words are interpreted as half a sentence: "To tell us that the police prevented him from going inside ...?" And page 56 the very bottom: "I believe him in that this is correct. But how am I supposed to believe him when he says 'the police didn't let me come and videotape.'" Now, if you turn over the page to page 57: "How can I believe you that the police told you couldn't come here to visit this place." Now, can I just be clear, Mr. Pappas. We've looked at Mr. Kaufmann's description in his book of your team being excluded and there being an argument. We've looked at the record in the Team Peje report for the 18th of September, referring to a small dispute with the prosecutor as to why the team wasn't allowed to see the evidence sooner. You didn't arrive there, you say, at the canal and the hotel until the 18th, but it seems that you are present here on a videotape taken on the 16th, before you told us you'd met Judge Cvejic. Can you just explain to us what you understand to have been going on?
For me, it's very simple. It might be a small mixing of information or dates, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, what does that mean?
That means maybe I met him one day before, and I don't remember that after eight years. It's like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But in your report written at the time, on the 5th of October, 1998, you record that it was the morning of the 17th where you first met him at the court.
Can you please read what I wrote --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I read it to you earlier. "On the morning of the 17th September, I visited the court of Pec to meet the local judiciary for the first time. I met the president of the court Mr. Zivadin Cvejic, as well as the public prosecutor Mr. Rade Gojkovic."
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, is that --
I met the local judiciary for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But unless the time --
I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and date counter on the videotape there is wrong, Mr. Pappas, you'd met him the day before and not at the court at all but in the yard of the KLA HQ in Gllogjan while there was a row going on about why the police had caused exclusion from the area?
I told you that it might be only a mixing of dates and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it's not just a mixing of dates on any view, is it, Mr. Pappas, it's a mixing of places?
No, it's not mixing of places.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't at the court you met him, was it? I mean, if this video shows it's earlier in time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could we first try to find out whether the witness remembers. Do you remember the event which was video-recorded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember now that I see it, but I wasn't remember it before and if you might ask me what date was that without seeing it, I wouldn't be able to refer at exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not asking you to refer to an exact date. Was it before you saw the bodies in Hotel Pastrik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was, yes, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was, from what we understand, on the 18th of September. Now, next question would be: Was it before you met with the judiciary, as you said, in -- I think you said it was in Pec?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If it was on 16th that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- that particular film?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was one day before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that's no answer to my question, because if it was the 16th, then of course it was the day before the 17th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That goes without saying. I'm asking you whether you remember whether you went there with the judiciary before you discussed matters in Pec?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot recall that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't recall that. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were shown and identified a photograph which was appended to your witness statement of the building that we've just seen with a pile of rubble outside it. Do you remember now when it was that you took that photograph?
I stated that I think it was 18th of September, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you go there twice?
Yes, we might be there twice. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, try and remember, if you can.
I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could we perhaps -- When you went to Hotel Pastrik, do you remember whether you went there --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recall that it was 18th of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My question is: Do you remember whether you went there directly or whether you went there first visiting other villages, such as Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall that, but I think we went directly there. Afterwards, we've been to the area that allegedly was the mass grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm still, if I may, just trying to explore with you the circumstances in which you seem to have been present on the 16th of September in Gllogjan whilst this argument was taking place. Do you recall now whether you had been to Gllogjan before going to the court in Pec?
After what I saw on video, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So was it wrong what you wrote to your government then, that the first time you met Judge Cvejic was on the 17th? Were you wrong in that because you'd actually met him the day before?
Wrong statement, yes, wrong -- wrong use of word, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And also wrong in your consolidated witness statement when you repeated the same thing and signed for it and told the Court yesterday that it represented the truth?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I object to that question, and Mr. Emmerson knows what this witness is saying. He's not suggesting that -- this witness is not saying that he was wrong in the sense that he lied in his statement. He said that he saw the video and having seen that video, he's agreeing with the propositions put by Mr. Emmerson concerning the 16th, and the question should be framed in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: One of the propositions I'm putting is that what is written in his Rule 92 ter statement, which was admitted yesterday, is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we heard the testimony of the witness today, we can read what is in his 92 ter statement. I think we have sufficiently heard now how the witness explains the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the question might not further assist in the matter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I -- can I ask this briefly: Do you remember now -- you say you see the video and it jogs your memory, do you remember now there being an argument about exclusion by the police of your team?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you remember there being an argument at all?
Talking with Kaufmann was always an argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Can we look behind tab 19 in the bundle, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, Mr. Emmerson, I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Keep an eye on the clock?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Remind you, yes, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I presume --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what you told us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have two very short documents to deal with, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, tab 19 is a record of a visit by Team Prizren to the canal itself on the 8th of September; in other words, it appears from tab 19 that ECMM Team Prizren visited the canal itself on the 8th of September. Did you know that that had happened?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And have you ever seen this document before?
No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where to look, exactly, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's from the top, from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The first -- the first two-thirds of that page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- is all about the visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we look at, for example, the second paragraph: "The team," that is Team Prizren, "observed a couple of houses and some haystacks burning while driving through the village of Gllogjan. The village appeared quite destroyed, 80 to 85 per cent. Serb police forces were conspicuously present wearing the yellow ribbons that denote stand-down alert." And then there is a reference to a briefing that was given at the scene by a Serb police representative. Now, with that in mind, if we could just turn behind tab 20, and I think this was mentioned briefly yesterday. May I just check if it's been marked for identification. Yes, it's P280 already. If we could just turn to the second page in that, and we look at page 4.3 -- paragraph 4.3.1. This is a report dated the 9th of September, so the day after Team Prizren visited the canal site. 4.3.1 reads: "KDOM Team Pristina and KDOM-US visited the alleged mass grave site 1 kilometre north of Gllogjan, 18 kilometres south/south-east of Pec. Representatives of the FRY Ministry of the Interior showed KDOM nine unidentified bodies." Now, were you aware of that?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we look two paragraphs further up, 3.2.1: "KDOM Team Pec was denied access by the Serb special forces to the alleged mass grave site in Rausic, Donji Ratis, and Prilep. Team Pec was not allowed to proceed towards Djakovica." Were you aware at any time that there were suggested mass grave sites at Prilep and Rausic, that the Serbs were suggesting that there had been mass grave sites found at Prilep and Rausic?
We used to hear a lot of rumours, but I don't remember this exact thing that you are showing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And as far as Donji Ratis is concerned, the reference to the special forces keeping Team Pec away from Donji Ratis, and are you aware of there being another grave site at Donji Ratis, apart from the canal?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And does this jog your memory about there being a process of your team being excluded?
No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because by the time you get there, the nine bodies that were seen by Team Prizren have become how many?
24 and plus some remains from other bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But none of them in situ when you got there?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Two final questions, if I may. Did the Serb officials who briefed you at Hotel Pashtrik, did they ever tell you that they found two complete, fully fleshed and very recently killed bodies floating in the water of the canal?
No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you have any means of comparing the photographs that were shown to you with the records of the Serbian post mortems, because you expressed the view that they were very convincingly explained? Did you ever make a comparison between the photographs and post-mortem records?
That's an express [sic] that Mr. Kaufmann did.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.
And I agreed to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So did you see a photograph of two bodies floating in the water?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you become aware at all at any stage that there were bodies that are shown in the photographs that had not been picked up or recorded by the Serb officials; that there was a discrepancy, in other words, between the photographic evidence and the records?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know that?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. And finally this: We've heard witness testimony in this court that a very short time before the Serb records show the discovery of this area, that there were a group of dead people, including a woman and a child, inside the cow-sheds at the economic farm. You went to the cow-sheds at the economic farm, didn't you?
Yes, we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And of course there were no bodies at the time that you went there; were there?
That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you ever told that the Serb authorities had found bodies inside the cow-sheds?
No, I don't recall that. Only on a ditch outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, are you ready to cross-examine Mr. Pappas?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. You'll now be cross-examined, Mr. Pappas, by Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, could you please tell us, when did you first arrive in Kosovo for purposes of this particular mission?
I don't recall the exact date but it was between 15th and 17th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At the time you arrived, I believe you told us that you were briefed by your team leader, Mr. Kaufmann, concerning the situation as he understood it to be; correct?
That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And how long a period of time had Mr. Kaufmann been in the region, to your knowledge?
To my knowledge, it must be two up to four months. I don't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the period of time that Mr. Kaufmann was briefing you about the situation, did he share with you at that point in time any of the previous reports that had been filed concerning the situation in Kosovo?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you arrived in Kosovo around the middle of July, you told us that you began patrolling the roads; correct?
That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you began patrolling the roads, what was your point of departure for patrolling those roads; by that I mean what city or village did you leave from?
All the time, we were living in Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during the period of time of your patrols, were you always using, for the first month that is, the services of the Albanian translator when you were dealing with Albanian issues, Mr. Kastriot?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Kastriot was a -- thank you -- was a tall man, was he not?
Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He had played basketball before working with you?
I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Would you say that Kastriot and Kaufmann were about the same height?
Almost, yes. A little bit, I think, taller was Kaufmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Kaufmann was a bit taller?
I think. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And Kastriot was -- he was a bit heavier, 20 to 30 kilos heavier; was he not?
Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Both of those gentlemen are considerably taller than you are, aren't they?
Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you tell us how tall you are?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "1.77," that's centimetres; correct?
Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. You, during the first week that you were in Kosovo, learned of a substantial sea change in terms of the Serbian activity with regard to attacking various areas; and by that I mean there was an offensive on the 25th of July in the Lapusnik region. You knew about that, didn't you?
I might not have started yet my patrols with the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

On 20th of July, but I don't recall that. I recall a lot of clashes, some of them very close to us, to the city of Pec I mean. But I don't recall each and every one of those and in any place, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you receive information around the 25th of July that there was a substantial Serbian attack in the Lapusnik gorge area?
We might. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you went out on patrol on a daily basis, did you educate yourself - and by that, I mean you personally - did you educate yourself about what the situation was on the ground so that you could make an intelligent determination about where to go?

First of all, this was something that Kaufmann was about to decide every day, and we were in a place that things were changing rapidly, even within the period of one day. So you couldn't know what you are going to face.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand that. Did you have the ability to contact other ECMM monitors to obtain information about what changes there may well be during any period of time that you were going to be out on patrol?

We had the -- the ability to contact with them, but most of the times we didn't, because we were working in different areas. A lot of things that we were seeing, they didn't; a lot of things they -- they knew or seeing, we could not be able to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So --
So only in case of a kind of emergency we would call each other to speak about something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And how would you characterise, for purposes of a discussion, an emergency? What constituted an emergency?
I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that a major Serb offensive in an area relatively close to where you were stationed would be something of moment and importance with regard to what you were going to be doing, your team was going to be doing?
I don't know. It's a hypothetical question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I understand your evidence correctly, you never received any such information from the time that you first arrived in Kosovo until August 11th; correct?
I didn't say we never received. I said that I never got knowledge of such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you what you knew.
Yeah, yeah, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. During the period of time that you were out on patrol during the month of July, did you visit Serb police stations as part of your observation and monitoring duties?
I'm not sure about the dates you are talking about in July or not, but we visited police station in Pec and also in Decani and of course Djakovica, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You told us yesterday when Mr. Emmerson asked you questions concerning weapons, the quality and quantity of weapons that you observed --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this, for the courtesy of Court and counsel, is page 4262.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- that most of the people that you saw were carrying old weapons. And then you went on to say - and this is what I'm interested in asking you about - "it seemed like the guns that from time to time we were seeing gathered in police stations they were finding in villages and stuff."
Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are these incidents, incidents where the Serb police were showing you collections of weapons that they had seized from Albanian villages?
Yes, from time to time I -- I can just recall a big collection of these kind of guns in Djakovica police station. They show us at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall, as you sit here today, how many times you saw that?
Maybe two, three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall if you saw that initially in the month of July?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall when you saw it, if ever, in the month of August?
No, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the mandate that you had, if I understood your testimony correctly, you could make a determination of what to evaluate and what to report back to your headquarters; correct?
That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, when you were doing that, when you were trying to make a determination of what factual information was of importance, did you have some guidelines that you used?
You mean if we had the specific task from time to time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.
That's something that used to happen in Bosnia when I were, but in Kosovo, no, we had an open ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: An open what?
We didn't have something specific to -- to report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'm not objecting but I'm trying to follow the evidence, and it seems to me that counsel and the witness were at cross-purposes. Mr. Guy-Smith asked if this witness had guide-lines to determine what information's important, what's not. Then the witness asked if he had a specific task, specific job. It's a different thing. Guide-lines are one thing and being given a specific job is another. I just wonder --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, the witness sought verification of whether he understood the question well. By rephrasing it and perhaps not saying exactly the same, but Mr. Guy-Smith said that that's how the question should be understood. So, therefore, I think we could continue on that basis. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you -- when you said you -- you had an open, that you didn't have something specific to report, how did you and your colleagues make a determination of what information you were going to report to the headquarters?

As far as I understood when I arrived there, from Kaufmann, he briefed me about the area. So he told me something also about reporting. He said to me that we supposed to report everything we see, and then it's up to the others to decide what they are going to investigate and to ask for more details or whatever. That's what we are doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I take it that's -- that's what you did during the period of time that you were working with Kaufmann; correct?
Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you keep a daily log or report of what you saw and experienced?
You mean, personally? Me, myself?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I mean you, yourself, sir.
No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, may I seek some clarification. You said you would report whatever you observed and then you would wait whether there would be any further questions. Now, if I try to imagine what it takes to report everything I see every day, that I need three days off to report that. For example --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Besides --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- price of bread. If you see any change, would you report that? Or was it focusing on military matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For example, Your Honour, we would report an unrest due to population because they have a fear of something that will happen. But we -- we wouldn't expect this to happen and then to report something. Something like that, yes, we would but not the bread pricing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So everything that you observed to -- that might be relevant for --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To be all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- tensions --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. To be out of normal, let's say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From our point of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But mainly then focusing on -- on not only military matters but on security matters --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- unrest in society rather than economic matters or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Humanitarian maybe, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was one of the matters that you were to report on the movement of the civilian population as a result of the unrest or military engagement that you observed?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Apart from the incident that you've testified to here today that you saw on the 11th of August, did you report any other incidents regarding the movement of the population as a result of unrest because of military engagements?

Yeah. We reported sometimes even rumours that we used to hear or whatever you -- we were able to see. For example, I remember a case in Krusevac, I don't recall the exact day, that a lot of internal displaced persons were gathered because of conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going to move to the 11th of August now. The first thing that I'd like to discuss with you, depending on how the time that the Court intends on taking the break, is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The break will be within the next -- somewhere within the next five minutes. If you are able to finish with the photograph within that time, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could see Exhibit 272.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The exhibit -- that's the photograph of his -- of the car that Mr. Pappas testified that he was driving, that he said was taken sometime in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Looking at that photograph, I note that there is on the side of what seems to be some insignia, a blue square?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that insignia an insignia that was on other parts of the vehicle on August 11th?
Yes. There was another flag on the other side of the car at the same position at the door of co-driver. There was one more, I don't know the English word for this, on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Hood?
On the hood, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: On the hood?
And one at the back door of the car. One could see it if you were standing behind the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you testified that at one point an individual was attempting to take these decals off of the car?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us which of the decals the individual was attempting to take off of the car? And I understand we only have one that can be seen on the driver's-side door, but was it on the hood? Was it on the passenger side?
It was the one on the driver's side, and a small Greek flag that I told you before at the back and even the one you can see in orange-like colour letters on the top frame of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Just for purposes of the record, since there may be some concern about hood. The hood is the part of the car that covers the engine in a front-wheel drive vehicle?
Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to make sure that every -- that we're all on the same page.
Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have the decal on the driver's-side door replaced at some point in time before you had this picture taken?
What do you mean "decal"?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The insignia that's on the driver's-side door.
Yes, as far as I remember we have it -- we had it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "we had it," is that in the same condition that it was in on the 11th of August?
I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is the insignia on the driver's-side door, as we see it in this photograph, in the same condition that it was after the time when you said an individual was attempting to take the insignia off the car?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm done with that particular exhibit at this time, and I've been more than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me -- yes. Your question, but please correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Guy-Smith. You started your question with an attempt to take the decal from the car and then later you asked whether it was replaced. I'm not quite certain anymore whether there's any evidence that it actually was taken from the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not either, which is why I asked whether or not it was in the same condition in the photograph that it is in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. So that's -- so that was a possibility that there was even no need to replace?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Possibility there was no need to replace it, which is something I can deal with after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know how important and how relevant that will be, but we'll hear from you. Mr. Pappas, we'll have a break until quarter past 4.00 and -- but I'm first inviting Mr. Usher to escort you out of the courtroom so that I can try to find more information about the time still needed, a matter certainly not of your concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, Mr. Harvey, Mr. Di Fazio, is there any reason to fear that we would not finish today, as we said yesterday we would expect?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: None whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have a break until quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to first discuss two scheduling matters. Mr. Emmerson has requested not to sit on the -- from the 5th until the 13th of July. We have not heard any specific position taken by the Prosecution, Mr. Di Fazio. At the same time, it was an urgent matter. Mr. Emmerson indicated why it was that he asked for not sitting and also why it was urgent. Mr. Emmerson, the Chamber, in the absence of any opposition, any objection by the Prosecution, until now is considering not to sit on Monday, the 9th; Tuesday, the 10th; Wednesday, the 11th; Thursday, the 12th. And then to see whether on the 5th of July, we could, perhaps, focus on procedural matters or at least not on, could I say, core evidence matters. We already decided that we would not sit usually on Fridays, that would take the 6th off as well. Would that do, as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's more than generous, and I'm extremely grateful for the flexibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's generous for you, Mr. Emmerson, because The Chamber has considered urgent matters it would have to do itself as well. So therefore it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There's no interpretation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no interpretation. Then everyone is on the right channel? Yes, I do understand there's interpretation now. Just to avoid whatever misunderstanding, urgent matters you may have elsewhere usually will not seduce the Chamber to give up sitting days. It was mainly because the Chamber needs some time to consider a lot of matters relevant to this case and rather do that not the last few days before the recess but do that one week prior to that, so if need be that we could address these issues on the week -- in the week after that. So it's not a matter of generosity, but I would say concurring interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, this is just to discourage any further requests of this kind, unless you have first inquired into what the Chamber needs. Then, Mr. Guy-Smith, it seems that you asked about the 5th and the 6th of June where the Limaj case will be heard on appeal. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. But before I ask for any decision, the matter right now is in quite a state of flux because of the potential health concerns of my client, which I'll be attending to immediately after trial today. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- I'll come back -- I'll come back with a specific request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith, I can tell you already that as part of other conversations with other Trial Chambers, that the Chamber is -- has already met a request of the Appeals Chamber to give up either the 5th or the 6th, and has decided that we would give up the 6th of June. You have not been informed about that yet. That is because I think it was the 15th of June, which is a - let me just have a look - is a Friday. The nonsitting day in the week 11 until the 15th of June, we might want to swap that - I don't know whether I indicated that earlier already - from the 15th to the 11th, that is, not sitting on the Monday. At the same time, there is a request outstanding whether we could swap the 15th from afternoon to morning, and we have not received an answer to that yet. This is just to inform you about some pending matters in relation to court scheduling. Mr. Harvey, I saw that you were on your feet as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just wanted the Court to be aware that I am Mr. Guy-Smith's co-counsel in the Limaj appeal, and so obviously the matter affects this trial in both ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course -- let's wait and hope for the best as far as the health concerns is -- and then, of course, what to do on the 5th and the 6th, whether you could split up or divide functions, that's, of course -- you still have to see to what extent we could save the 5th; if there's no possibility, then, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I've also had a brief conversation with Mr. Re about this with regard to what witnesses he may be calling, and there may be a way of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- of covering it -- covering it that way, too. So I'm trying to cover the base in any way I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's exactly the type of action the Chamber would expect you to take under those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One of the possible solutions would also be that we would -- where on the 5th of June, the Appeals Chamber will hear the Limaj case in the afternoon, whether we could -- oh, it's already -- already in the morning. Then Judge Hoepfel is better aware of the matter than I am. Then I think we could ask the usher to -- yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Just before we do that, I -- I think that we have a status on the issue of the translation of the four-page Greek document. I've been informed by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- Mr. Di Fazio that the document has been forwarded to the translation department, and that it is expected to be translated no earlier than Friday and maybe Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So -- you mean of Mr. Pappas, the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Then I'm afraid we have to wait and see what happens, if there would be any need to -- for a recall of Mr. Pappas at a later stage, we have to see that. But in view of what happened yesterday and in view of the time Mr. Pappas spent already in The Hague, I think it would be fair not to wait for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm in total agreement with that. I should inform the Chamber that I do intend to ask him about the one area that he did say that he relied upon in refreshing his memory concerning that document, which was the height of the individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Which, I believe, he indicated was a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course you could ask him. I take it that he still has a copy of that, and he knows what is in it. So questions can be asked about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that there's a certain amount of tidying up still to be done in terms of cross-referencing the tabs in the bundle to exhibit numbers on the record. The message that's come through to me from -- from the Bench is that Your Honour would like to postpone the tidying-up exercise until the very end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, for -- yes, until the very end, and perhaps even until Madam Registrar replaces again Mr. Registrar. What we would like to have is at the end -- you see, Mr. Di Fazio, that Madam Registrar has given you a list of documents in the range you intend to tender which have received already numbers. I very much would like to have the index of the bundle, but then completed with all the information we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as what MFI numbers, what is already admitted earlier, so that we have a full set of documents and then go --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly. The only ones that are not immediately available to be clarified are those which were to be collectively exhibited by Mr. Di Fazio, and I think those numbers are available. Whilst we are on the subject, can I just mention one document which is behind tab 28 which I haven't taken time asking the witness about because it doesn't seem to me likely that he'll have personal knowledge of it, but Your Honours may remember there being significance in the date upon which two individuals who are named in that document, that's the very last page in the bundle of the English translation. There is a significant -- I don't ask you to read the names because a protected witness is related to them, but Your Honours may recall that became of some significance as to the date of disappearance because it fixed the evidence of Witness 21 as to when it was he visited the canal site in relation to that. And this is an ECMM document recording information provided by the family as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are you seeking to have it tendered from the bar table?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It will be tendered from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we'll hear at that moment whether there's any objection. If you would include that in your --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in your index.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So might I ask Mr. Registrar to mark that individual document for identification, now, so it can have an identification number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Has it been uploaded in the system?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is uploaded in the system. It's part of a much larger document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's part of 65 ter 660.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have given it a number -- let me just have a look 28 is -- yes, there's no document ID for the Defence. It's part of 660 but wouldn't it be wise to have it uploaded, but the relevant portion, and not more than that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As it happens the whole of 660 is uploaded and I have selected one page from others that are irrelevant and I'm simply asking that that one page be marked for identification. Is that not a convenient way to do it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do we know which page that would be?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Within this document it is I think paginated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is -- well, of course we have the R numbers on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you would like to have the cover page?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is R025-9116, and the relevant page would be then R025-9118. These two pages together to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- attributed an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, these will be marked for identification as D67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The only matter - but I leave that to you, Mr. Emmerson - the cover page is only in English. The other page is translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We would then have one piece of evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which is not in the language of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm happy to take responsibility for that and have it translated for the benefit of the accused. The reason it's important is because there's a date error --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- on the subsequent document which plainly refers to events that took place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll come to that at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's at least marked now for identification and you include this number on your index when completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we could ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. And a final couple of questions with regard to the decal. Was that decal removed from your car on the 11th?
That's what I think. I'm not sure about this, you know, the tense of the moment and it's a lot of years ago, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's a detail you don't recall?
No. I think it was removed, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The person who you believe did that, is the same individual who you have told us hit and kicked your interpreter Mr. Kastriot?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have described him as an individual: slim, dark hair, dark complexion, and the height of 1 metre, 70 centimetres; correct?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you were able to determine his height because, as a matter of fact, you were standing close to him at one point during this incident?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is information that you recorded in your report to the Greek Embassy; correct?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, during the time that this man was beating Kastriot, Kastriot was fending off those blows and was actually talking to that man, wasn't he?
He was trying to, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And there came a point in time before anybody entered the room where that particular individual stopped hitting Kastriot; right?
He stopped hitting him before we were ordered to climb the stairs and go to the other floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Kastriot was considerably taller than this particular person, was he not, the man who was hitting him?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Would you say it would be fair to say that he was a couple of heads taller; and by that, I mean a good 10 to 15 centimetres taller?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the man who was -- was hitting Kastriot was, in fact, shorter than you are?
Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you had an opportunity to go on the ICTY web site and take a look at a number of pictures; correct?
Not a number, just those that I printed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Just the three pictures that you told us you've printed: one of Mr. Haradinaj, one of Mr. Balaj, and one of Mr. Brahimaj?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And those pictures were pictures that you saw after you had received information, I believe it was from your government, that you had been requested to testify against these men; correct?
Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did at any point in time any member of the Prosecution or an investigator come to you before you received that invitation to come testify and ask you to view a photo line-up?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Apart from the description that you have given us of the one man who was beating the interpreter, did you give any other descriptions of individuals that you saw that day on the 11th of August?
No, only his description and Haradinaj's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. After Mr. Haradinaj spoke with you, you were driven away, you were escorted, as I understand it, by, as you told us, among others, the man you've identified as Idriz Balaj; right?
That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the period of time that you were on the road, do you recall what villages you went through?
No, I just recall that we've been moving north from the way almost that we came.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you were -- when you parted company, they left you in the village of Ljumbarda, did they not?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You don't have any doubt about that, do you, that when these three men left you after this incident, you were left in the village of Ljumbarda, where you then had further discussions with other KLA members?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One question, Mr. Guy-Smith. In one -- line -- page 55, line 2, you said: "You were driven away," which I understand to be passive, that someone drives you somewhere. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I meant passive from the standpoint that he was in a car that was being driven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I did not understand him to be the driver of the car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, that's then understood. Is that how you understood the question as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, that's -- for that clarification. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Pappas. During your time in Kosovo, did you keep a diary of your day-to-day activities?
No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You didn't maintain a journal of any sort?
Not in Kosovo, not in Bosnia. That was before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Okay. How frequently during your time in Kosovo did you send incident reports to the Greek government?
I sent these two reports that you saw --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes.
-- until now, and another one that was about the cars we're using, logistics, problems, that they supposed to -- to take care about with other countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So just three reports during your entire time in Kosovo?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Okay. You took the trouble to go on to the ICTY web site in April of 2006 to look at and download the photographs of the three accused in this case. Did you -- and you took the trouble to bring those with you to the Tribunal when you came to meet with the Prosecutors earlier this month. That's correct, isn't it?
That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you bring with you any other documents, apart from those photographs, when you came to meet with the Prosecutor earlier this month?
The report that I delivered two days ago, one and a half, let's say, and the other one that I have delivered to Prosecutors when I arrived also.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So those are the only documents that you had with you as you were preparing your composite statement for presentation to the Tribunal this month?
Yeah, and some photos also.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And at the time when you gave your statement in May of 2006, did you have any other notes or reports to which you referred at that stage?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In your, what we call, 92 ter statement, that's the one that you made this month, you refer to both Mr. Haradinaj and to Mr. Balaj. You do not mention Mr. Brahimaj in that statement. Is there a reason for that?
The reason is that he was not part of the incident, as I say. An active part, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, I want to pursue this with you a little further, and just so you understand where I'm coming from, Mr. Pappas, it is my suggestion and my case that you have made a mistake and a very common mistake in that you have identified him inaccurately, wrongly, as having been present at the scene. You understand where I'm coming from on this?
Yeah -- yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, you told Mr. Guy-Smith just now that you only gave two descriptions of men whom you saw at the scene, that's the description of Mr. Haradinaj and Mr. Balaj; correct?
That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In May of 2006 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'm at paragraph 21 of the statement on page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- you said that Lahi Brahimaj was with the group in the compound where you were detained but - and these were your words - "he didn't do anything." You agree with that?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You said a little earlier in that statement, at paragraph 19, that: "There were at least 15 armed people, all of them in uniform." Is that correct?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When you say "at least 15," do you think it's more than 15?
More or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, "at least" implies not less, doesn't it?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So do you think it's more?
Might be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And approximately how long were you in the courtyard before you were taken upstairs to a room?
Some minutes, maybe five minutes tops.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So there was just a crowd of people, none of whom did anything to make them stand out as an individual in the crowd; correct?
That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And common sense, to which you've referred a number of times in the course of your testimony, common sense would tell you that when people are all in uniform, they are harder to tell apart than people who are dressed differently. Would you agree with that?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And would you agree also that in a situation such as the one that you have described, common sense tells you that you focus on the people who are talking or acting much more than you do on those who are just standing around?
That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you accept, of course, that it was almost eight years after the event that you first saw a photograph of my client, Mr. Brahimaj?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And that was just a photograph of his face and his head and shoulders with him wearing a suit and a shirt and tie?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Oh, the people in uniforms, what did they have on their heads?
Most of the times they had this hat, I don't know the word in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, like a beret?
Like a beret, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did these individuals have berets?
Not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Or did they have caps?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did any of them have anything on their heads?
The ones that I described or in general in the yard?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The ones in the yard in general.
Some of them, they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: After all this time, it is really impossible for you, isn't it, to be certain of the identities of anybody else in that yard?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'd like to make it clear, if I may, for the purpose of the record that I associate myself formally with the suggestion that Lahi Brahimaj was not present in Gllogjan on the 11th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if I -- if I might, I do the same and I had indicated earlier that my case was -- and perhaps there's one further question I should put to Mr. Pappas with the Chamber's permission, which would be the following: That he is mistaken that my client, Idriz Balaj, was the man who was beating the interpreter, Mr. Kastriot; however, he did see him on that day during that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. These are a couple of questions mixed up. Could you please separate them?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you put them. Let me first -- I want to be quite sure about the answer of what also was -- well, could be misunderstood. When you said "yes," Mr. Pappas, you confirmed that it was really impossible to be certain of the identities of anybody else in that yard, "anybody else" in this context meaning anybody else than specifically described by you. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a minute, to read exactly what he was asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I could repeat the question, but Mr. Harvey was seeking confirmation that you considered it impossible after all those years to recognise him. Is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
