utterances.text: I consider impossible to -- to give description of anybody that was in the yard, of course, but for the people that were acting or -- that's why I can say that Mr. Brahimaj would be there because maybe he was very close, so I remember the face. It was not something that -- or some person that I would meet a lot of times. So I could mix places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, there might be some misunderstanding, Mr. Harvey. Could you please further explore the matter? I just wanted to be sure that this "yes" was well understood by the Chamber, which supposes that the question was well understood by the witness. And I'm not fully convinced that there is no confusion at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour. I think there may have been some confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, you've had the experience, haven't you, if in your ordinary daily life, that you've walked down the street and you've seen somebody on the other side of the road and you have thought for certain that you recognised them and then a moment later you realised that you're completely mistaken; correct?
That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I'm talking there in terms of recognising somebody familiar to you, somebody who you know. You can mistakes, can't you, like that?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, it's very clear that you have never seen Mr. Brahimaj on any occasion, other possibly than on the occasion you're talking about on the 11th of August. You never saw him before that date, did you?
No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You've never seen him since that date?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Until you came into court today?
That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And so it comes to this, that for something -- for a few minutes, during which a group of people are standing there, all in uniform, none of them doing anything to make them stand out, you have singled out from a photograph you saw eight years later the third person who is accused in this case and you have said, Ah, yes, that was one of the crowd. That's what it comes to, isn't it?
I would say that his face came to me, yes, and it was connected with this incident in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you consider yourself to be a fair and objective man, sir?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Being fair, being objective, do you think that there is a possibility that you just might be mistaken?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you've heard counsel for the two other defendants both say that their client's position is yes they were there but that my client was not. Do you think that you may really be mistaken after of all these years?
Maybe after all these years, yes. There is a slight possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think it's as far as I can take it, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Here again the answer the slight possibility. I mean, everyone would say even of what happened five minutes ago a slight possibility then we have to explore is that a theoretical possibility. Mr. Pappas, just a simple question to you after all the questions Mr. Harvey has put to you: Are you positive, are you certain, that the person you saw on the internet that person -- that picture on the internet being a photograph of Mr. Brahimaj in this courtroom, are you certain beyond, I would say, doubt that is automatically and always in one's mind, but are you certain that he was in the courtyard, yes or no --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's a clear answer. That's -- Mr. Harvey. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: To make this round of clarifications complete. May I ask you, please, Witness, if this was one sentence or it was two sentences. You said a while ago, it is on transcript 61, line 18 and 19: "It was not something that -- or some person that I would meet a lot of times, so I could mix places." It has been written down now as two sentences --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's one sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Some person that I would meet a lot of times, so I could mix places, this is one sentence, a coma before the word "so" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, is there any need for re-examination? Perhaps before giving an opportunity, the Chamber is always at least -- at least I'm always a bit hesitant to put questions first or last. I would have one very specific question which, I don't know whether it would have any bearing on the questions you have in mind. Could we have P279 on the screen? Could it be enlarged? Let me just -- Mr. Emmerson, there was somewhere in the tabs. Do you remember which tab it was so that I can look at the hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was the -- yes, it may have been 25, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not -- it's not 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, it's not there, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just -- in this -- oh, first of all, we should go into -- should we go into private session for this matter or was this the report that was -- I'm not quite sure. Mr. -- I know that there were -- not all of the reports were under seal, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But this one is?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll go for a second into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption, Your Honours, but we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. If Your Honours please, perhaps before I ask any questions in re-examination, Mr. Guy-Smith raised earlier - and I'm looking at page 60 - there's -- he said there's one further question I should put to Mr. Pappas with the Chamber's permission, which would be the following: That he's mistaken that my client, Idriz Balaj, was the man who was beating the interpreter Mr. Kastriot; however, he did see him on that day during that time. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- in the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Di Fazio, to cut matters short, I interrupted Mr. Guy-Smith at that time because I wanted to be sure about the answer the witness gave to the last question of Mr. Harvey. After having clarified the issue raised by Mr. Harvey, I did not, which I should have done, have given an opportunity to Mr. Guy-Smith to finish what he was doing when I interrupted him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And if Your Honours please -- I understand that. And if Your Honours please, I don't know what Mr. Guy-Smith's intentions are, but I submit that he should ask that question, give the opportunity to the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if I'm giving the opportunity, if he doesn't do it, then it's time to consider what he should do, but if he does it. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm more than happy to take the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, I suggest to you that you are mistaken when you say that the individual who was beating your interpreter, Mr. Kastriot, was Idriz Balaj, the man that you identified after looking at the photographs on the web of the ICTY, that you're wrong about that, you've made a mistake.
Do you want an answer to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do.
No, I'm sure he was the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I further suggest to you that you did see him on that day. You saw him at least on two occasions, one during the time that you were with all these people, the people who were in the yard, and during the time that Mr. Kastriot was being beaten, and also when he escorted you to safety.
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Even there, there's some ambiguity. Mr. Guy-Smith, in the second question, asked you that you did see him on that day in the yard and escorting you away. Since your testimony is that he was in the yard beating the interpreter, it's difficult to understand how you could say no to having seen him in the yard. So therefore, it's not fully clear to me what your answer is. Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The answer, Your Honour, is that I stand for my statements just now, that he was the one, he beated the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He's the one who drive us in the village for -- from first place and drive us out of the village afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the answer is that you are pertinent in saying that you saw him beating your interpreter, that he was then in the yard, and that he escorted you in and out of Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then having clarified this, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You were asked if a photo line-up was ever provided to you before -- during this afternoon by Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith. Before you actually accessed the ICTY web site, had you had a chance to speak to any -- any investigator from this institution?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked a number of questions yesterday concerning Serb artillery and location of Serb positions and the activities of Serb forces in and around the lake. In all the time that you were there in Kosovo, in this area, did you ever have an opportunity to see or lay eyes on Serb artillery positions?
No, at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. As a -- all right. You didn't see anything. Did you have any information as to the sort of artillery being used by Serb -- by the Serb forces, what calibre, what potency and what range?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there anything from the shell explosions that you heard and saw on the 11th of August that led you to conclude what sort of calibre or power this artillery had?

We found in another place where was the -- the photograph of our car, if you remember, it was a burnt house next to it, we found there some big shells of artillery with Cyrillic, how you say, this alphabet of Serbian language on it. And it -- I've been told that it was a shell of 120-millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's --
That's the only time I ever see from these kind of shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Speaking as a military man, that's a pretty large calibre, isn't it?
It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know the range of 120-millimetre shells?
No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that any different, apart from whether that's -- I'm not an expert, but whether it's 120-millimetre mortar, which I understand is considered to be artillery, or whether it would be any other weapon that would fire that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only artillery. You would see by the shell of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The word "shell" meaning exactly what, that what lands or that what remains if what fired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that that's called a cartridge, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shell-case. Yes, you see, I learned a lot. So you saw shell cases --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- belonging to 120-millimetre ammunition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, thank you for answering my questions and the questions of other counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The shell-casings that you've been answering questions about, where was it that you saw them?
It was for sure in another area, but I cannot recall the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you give us some idea, please, where it was? You showed -- told us about a photograph that was taken at the same place. Where were the shell-casings, roughly?
I was, I believe, on the other side when we visited this empty villages --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On the other --
-- we found on the -- on the way, on the main road from Pec to Pristina and a little bit south of those main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And presumably if they're empty cases with Cyrillic, it was that which caused you to conclude that they were Serb shells?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when a shell is fired from a heavy weapon, the casing is discharged from the weapon at the position where the weapon is fired from. Is that correct?
I'm not sure if it's automatic -- automatically rejected from the weapon, but -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's either rejected automatically or removed by the operator of the weapon and left in the position from which the weapon had been fired?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the casings you saw were evidence in your mind that the Serb forces had fired from that position?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I don't have any supplementary questions arising from that cross-examination, if Your Honours please, and I can say that my re-examination is now over. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's how I understood it, and I understood it also that Mr. Emmerson did put this question because it was triggered very specifically by the question you put to the witness in re-examination. That's how I understand the procedural situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Bench has no further questions, and since the -- as Mr. Di Fazio noticed, the Defence is usually alert enough to not wait for an invitation. I take it that Mr. Guy-Smith and Mr. Harvey have no further questions either?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pappas, this then concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for having come to The Hague, especially since the Chamber, of course, is aware of the inconvenience it caused you to stay for a third day of giving evidence. We wish you a safe and a quick trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Pappas out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest to the parties that we'll finally deal with the exhibits once we have finalised the indexes, schedules, and whatever it is, filled in with every detail, and then deal with it. That would perhaps be after Madam Registrar has returned. Then, Mr. Di Fazio, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I think I might leave that question to Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: My prediction is that he's going to say yes, they are ready, but I'll leave that to Mr. Kearney as to whether we are ready to call our next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kearney, that raises another issue of whether it will be better -- I take it that in view of proofing sessions often held prior to a witness appearing in this courtroom, you would know better whether it would serve the witness to start with the examination-in-chief for the, well, let's say, 15 minutes, then have a break, and then to finish in the remaining 45 minutes, or whether you think it would be better for the witness to have a break now and then to ask him -- that you call him after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I think taking a break now would be a good idea, Your Honour, just to allow us to get set up and have him to come into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have a break until 20 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Kearney, no protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Good afternoon, Mr. Cekaj. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then before you give -- before you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, Mr. Cekaj. We -- of course, we get what you say translated in English, and we can hear you. Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by the usher, and I'd like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Honourable Judges, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Cekaj. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, you'll be first examined by Mr. Kearney, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Kearney, did you explain, because I do understand that you would like to have a 92 ter statement admitted. Have you explained to Mr. Cekaj how this works?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed, and also explain to the Chamber exactly what the 92 ter statement is in this case. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, good afternoon. Thank you for coming to The Hague and --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- and thank you for your patience. First before we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: With the Trial Chamber's permission, before we get into the 92 ter, I'd like to identify this witness formally for the record, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, I wonder if you could state your full name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Shemsedin Cekaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Could you please tell us both your date of birth and your place of birth, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I was born on the 23rd of May, 1958, in Irzniq, of Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And what is your father's name?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Osman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And lastly, could you tell us what your current occupation is and what languages you speak?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I am a member of the Kosova Protection Corps, and I am chief of operations in the guard of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And I'll ask you, sir, what languages do you speak?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I speak Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cekaj. Mr. Cekaj, last week on the 9th and 11th of May, 2007, did you provide a statement here in The Hague to the Prosecution which was reduced to writing?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And after that document was made, were you given an Albanian translation of that to read on your own and make corrections to?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did you do that, Mr. Cekaj? Did you read the document in Albanian, make corrections, and have those corrections incorporated into a final document?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After that process, were paragraphs from that longer statement put into a shorter statement for your review as well?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And were you shown an Albanian copy of that document as well?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And after being given that document, did you -- after making sure it was accurate, did you sign it and then initial all the pages of that document?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time with the Trial Chamber's permission, I'd like to show this witness 65 ter Exhibit 1339, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. It needs a -- could you tell us what it exactly is? Is that the 14th of May statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This is the 14th of May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. That's clear. That needs a number to be assigned to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll mark that for identification as P317.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are you going to show the hard copy to the witness or to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: It was not my intent to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The electronic copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I just wonder if we can scroll down far enough so the witness can see his signature at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please look at your screen, Mr. Cekaj. That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, I would like to ask you, is that a copy of the document you signed on the 14th of May, the shorter statement that we talked about earlier?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that is the one, this is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature at the bottom of that first page?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Does this document, Mr. Cekaj, reflect what you would say in court today if you were questioned about these same topics?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, with the -- what's the original and what's the translation? Is the English the original or is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I believe -- are they all -- is the Albanian and English included in this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The one you just showed to the witness is just the Albanian front page, from what I see. You asked him about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: May I have one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I said earlier appears to be the case, that this 65 ter number contains both the Albanian and the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but nevertheless I would like to know what you consider to be the original and what to be the translation. I'll explain to you why. Perhaps we -- perhaps I start doing that. Could a -- could we look at paragraph 25 of this? Could that be on the screen, that's the page 9? Could we zoom-in? Mr. Cekaj, would you be so kind to read the first sentence of paragraph 25, as it appears on your screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I returned from a meeting in Irzniq on the 7th of July, around 5.00 in the morning, on the 8th of July. Late in the morning somebody informed me that the Serb forces had attacked Loxha from the Peje side. However, we did not go there because we received information that other forces had gone to Loxha to reinforce them."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I, first of all, seek clarification by the interpreters whether there's a chance that there was a misinterpretation as we returned from a meeting from Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No, that's what the witness read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what -- yes. Mr. Kearney, the reason why I'm raising this issue is the following: Cutting and pasting is a dangerous exercise. If you look at the earlier statement, the -- well, let's say the -- I think the 9th to 11th of May statement, then you find -- I think it's in paragraph 41, but just -- yes. On page 41 -- paragraph 41, you find a description of a meeting in lower Lluka, yes. Now, in paragraph 25 of the new statement, the English text reads that: "I returned from a meeting held on the 7th of July in lower Lluka." That might well be the case, but the Albanian text doesn't say anything in paragraph 25 on where that meeting was held. So apart from what seems now to be an additional problem on whether he was returning from or to Irzniq, at least lower Lluka is introduced in a mysterious way, not to say that it's not correct, but at least we now see that the Albanian and the English version, at least in this respect, are not the same. And it seems that something from the earlier statement slipped in, I don't know inspired by whom, in the English version; where the version the witness could read doesn't contain any such information. That's the reason why I was asking what is the original -- it might well be that this is just one single mistake. Of course, I couldn't check all of the Albanian, and I'm not inclined to do so. But cutting and pasting seems to be the new practice. Have a larger statement, and extract a bit of it. And here we see that suddenly in the extract, that we get information which is, at least in the two languages, not the same, and that is of some concern. The Chamber very much appreciates high precision in every respect. I leave it up to the parties whether there's anything more of the kind. I've got no idea, but this is what just caught my eye and I'd like to bring that to your attention. We'll finally give a decision on whether it will be admitted or not but first give an opportunity to the Defence to further check. I tried, as a matter of fact, to see whether that was the same in the Albanian version of the 9th to the 11th of May, but we are provided only with the English. So therefore, I do not know if there are any problems there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps to circumvent this issue right now, we can -- Prosecution can move on, not tender this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- well, I take it you can -- it's now 20 lines on the record, so I do not mind -- it's clear to everyone now that there at least is a bit of a problem. Let's move on, but this is just again an exercise which is aiming at highest precision possible. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Your Honour, between today and tomorrow, we can revisit this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: We'll look at that document again, but thank you for calling that to the Prosecution's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, I want to direct your attention, if I may, back to late March of 1998. I want to ask you, sir, at that time where were you living?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: At the end of March 1998, I was living in Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Sir, as of that time, late March of 1998, had you as yet joined the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I had not joined the KLA at that time, at the end of March 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to ask you, Mr. Cekaj, at that time, even as a civilian, were you aware of any military activity taking place in or around Peje?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. As a civilian, I had heard about Serbian forces that had attacked the Jashari family in Prekaze on the 5th, 6th, and 7th, and then the Haradinaj family on the 24th of March. And that was what inspired me to join the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, in addition to what you -- you heard through other people or in the media, did you actually physically observe, either with your own eyes or your own ears, from Peje military activity in late March of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us about that, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: There were many Serb forces in Peje, police forces, and paramilitary forces, other formations as well that used masks. They were trying to intimidate the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How about the sounds of any fighting? Were you aware of the sounds of any fighting in late March of 1998, from your home in Peje?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. You could hear shelling from Smolice and Gllogjan from positions where the Serb forces were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you say -- the translation read: "From Smolice and Gllogjan," I want to ask you, based on your hearing, were the -- where was the artillery that was causing the shelling stationed?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: They were shelling Smolice and Baballoq, Dubrave, up to the part in the beginning where the Serb forces were attacking with artillery and other weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, how often was this taking place, this is late March now of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: These were concentrated attacks, intensive attacks, with a certain intensity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, could you please seek clarification on the basis of hearing, from what I understood your question to be, from Peje, exact locations at a distance of quite a number of kilometres raises some additional questions. Could you please clarify that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, this shelling you've talked about, is this -- first of all, is this something that you actually heard with your own ears?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: When artillery fire is there, you can hear it. You can hear the shelling of heavy artillery. You can hear it from 2 or 3 kilometres away, even farther away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So from your -- you're living in Peje at the time, sir. From your home in Peje, could you hear the shelling?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: You could hear it from the street. I could hear it from my home where I lived. So we could hear the shelling, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You told us earlier that the shelling was directed towards several villages, I think you mentioned Baballoq, Smolice, Dubrave, and Gllogjan, how do you know that's where the shelling was directed?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. The villages of Smolice, Baballoq, Gllogjan, I could see them because I went illegally, I went in secret to my village to visit as well, but I could hear the shelling from Peje as well. But, as I said, I went to visit my village in secret several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, I'm being informed that there may be a translation issue at page 84, line 25, and that "2 or 3 kilometres" may be a mistranslation, and that the witness may have said "20 or 30 kilometres."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson, the proper way of doing it is saying that it is the distance the witness described, then we put the witness again to him, and then we'll hear what his evidence is --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Instead of giving -- if there's no mistranslation, then at least there is then a suggestion that that would be the -- perhaps the right answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You understand that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Clearly, the -- certainly, it was unintended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm not saying that you had bad intentions. When you said that you could hear -- let me just have it again. You said: "You can hear the shelling of heavy artillery, you can hear it from," and then you gave the number of kilometres, and you said: "Even farther away." How many kilometres you could hear from the shelling of heavy artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Peje and my village are 22 kilometres apart, while Gllogjan and other villages that were shelled are about 4 kilometres from my village. So all in all, 26 kilometres I would say, and you can hear them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This shelling that you're talking about, Mr. Cekaj, was it happening on a daily, a weekly, a biweekly, a monthly basis? Please tell us more about the -- the regularity of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Almost every day at certain intervals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And how about KLA activity during this period in late March of 1998, were you aware of any activity on the part of the KLA at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: At that time, the KLA had just started to organise in the villages that were under attack, after the event or the incident of the 24th in Gllogjan. So they organised themselves to defend their villages in the event of a Serb attack so that the Serbs would not penetrate into the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, I want to move on to a slightly different matter, if I may. I want to ask you if as of late March of 1998, you had ever actually met Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When was it that you first actually met Mr. Haradinaj, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I met Ramush Haradinaj for the first time in my village, in Irzniq, around mid-April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you remember the exact date of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date, but around the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, how was it -- or how did you travel to that meeting with Mr. Haradinaj from your village in Peje to Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Not from the village, from Peje. I think that was wrong. I established contact with Ramush Haradinaj through my brother, as I mentioned, and I travelled in my car, with my family, through the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, this is your April meeting with him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's the April meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, when you say "through the villages," did you -- there is a main road from Peje south towards Decane. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, there is a main road from Decane, but I did not follow that one. I followed another road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I went through Lybeniq, Strellc i Ulet, Pozhare, Kodrali, and my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, why is it that you chose not to use the main road but chose to go through the villages instead?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Because there were check-points, Serb check-points, and I feared to go through those check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How about in the roads that went through the villages, who controlled those roads at that time when you went from Peje to Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: In those villages there were young men, some wearing uniforms, some did not have uniforms, I mean of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: All those villages you mentioned earlier along that route from Peje to Irzniq, were there KLA soldiers, whether they were in uniform or out of uniform, in all those villages, Mr. Cekaj?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: In some of the villages from Irzniq to other villages, I -- that's where I saw some members of the KLA, in some of their check-points that they had, at the entrance of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And on your route from Peje to Irzniq, if you remember, what villages had KLA check-points and which ones did you go through?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I went from Strellc i Ulet, there was one in Strellc i Ulet, then Isniq, Lluka e Ulet, Pozhare, at the entrance to Kodrali, and Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, when you went to these check-points, were you allowed to pass through?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: At each check-point there was somebody who knew me, because I was a well-known person in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you -- were documents being required at those check-points at that time, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: No, there was no need because there were people of my age who knew me, and they were not alone there. There were other people circulating. I had no problem going through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And based on your experience with the -- with the KLA and your knowledge of the region, if you had not been known at that time, would you have required some kind of permission or document to travel through those check-points?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Had I been in their place, I would have asked for documents, but they were there for security purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And what kind of documents would have been asked for at that time at those check-points?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I don't think there were certain documents at the time, but after that time there were some kind of permissions given just for safety and security purposes so that they would not have problems in other check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: These are permissions that were given by the KLA to travel through these check-points. Is that -- is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, yes. By the local staff of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I want to move now, if we may, to the actual meeting itself with Mr. Haradinaj. This was, you said, approximately 20th -- the 20th of April of 1998. I want to ask you, Mr. Cekaj, where did this meeting take place, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: The meeting took place in my brother's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That was actually inside the village of Irzniq. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, in Irzniq, in my brother's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you meet with Mr. Haradinaj, the -- on the day of your arrival or had you been in the village for some period of time before you met him?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: The same day I arrived, I met Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you met him, was he alone or was he with someone?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: It was Ramush Haradinaj and Togeri, Idriz Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How were the men dressed at that time when you met them?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: They were wearing uniforms, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did these uniforms have UCK patches on them?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, they had KLA patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What colour were the uniforms at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: It was solid colour, dark colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you say "dark," was it a -- what type of dark shade?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: It looked like green, dark green.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Pistols, light weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, at that time when you were meeting the person you identified earlier as Togeri, had you ever seen this person before? Had you ever met him before?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: No. I hadn't met him before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you met him at this meeting on the 20th of April in Irzniq, how did he introduce himself to you? What name did he go by? Was it a formal name or a nickname? What name did he give to you?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: You're asking about the Toger, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: The first contact was the introduction. We did not know each other before, so first I presented myself, then Ramush Haradinaj and Toger. That was his pseudonym, Toger.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So the name that you were -- that this Toger introduced himself to you as was actually Toger. Is that a -- is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At some point after that, Mr. Cekaj, did you learn his real name?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Not there, but later, not at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How much later did you learn his real name?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I think maybe after two months or three, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And what was his real name, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: His name is Idriz Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During your first conversation with the gentleman who identified himself as Toger, who you've identified as Mr. Balaj, did you discuss with him his level, if any, of military experience?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: We discussed very briefly. I asked him whether he was an officer by profession. He told me that he had some experience from the war in Croatia, nothing else. That was very brief. It was a very short conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, at this meeting itself that you had with Mr. Haradinaj and Mr. Balaj, how long did it last?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: It continued about one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What was discussed, please, if you could tell us during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: First, as I said, we introduced each other. I introduced myself to Ramush Haradinaj and Idriz Balaj. It was very correct conversation. We talked about the situation, about the difficult situation. At that time, the people was in a difficult situation. We shared similar opinions about the situation, so this was the essence of what we talked all the time. So we talked about how we could organise better. We had similar opinions about the situation which prevailed, about the situation in which the people were at that time. The people were on the eve of an unprecedented disaster. So these were all the things which I wanted to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you discuss the --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: This was the essence of the conversation. It was a very correct conversation, and I accepted with enthusiasm to have that conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you discuss the state of fighting in the Dukagjin Zone generally at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: It was a situation -- also during the meeting we heard shots from all kinds of weapons, from the place where --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Only to be perfectly accurate, I don't believe it was a defined Dukagjin Zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't believe that the question asked by Mr. Kearney is -- is accurate with regard to the time; that there was, in fact, at the time of this discussion a recognised Dukagjin Zone. So it's a mischaracterisation of the area at that time, and I just want to make sure that it doesn't lead to -- lead to any confusion later on in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we heard -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps, more particularly, it's a mischaracterisation of the testimony of this witness as recorded in his own statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, we heard evidence about zones also within the Dukagjin area. We have heard evidence about the Dukagjin Plain. Could you please try to keep this as clear as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'll re-ask the question. I'm not quite sure how to be more accurate, Your Honour, beyond to say:

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, did you discuss the state of fighting at that time on the - I'll use the word - Dukagjin Plain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think the Dukagjin Plain was exactly --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: If that makes it more clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what was established later. At least, that's the first impression the evidence gives. Perhaps you describe the area. In the area of villages so-and-so-and-so --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Or, indeed, in the Dukagjin area. It's a geographical region of Kosovo. The word "zone" is what is -- is what is the concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that seems to refer rather to operations than -- so "area" perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm happy to use that word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And it's not my intent to refer to any kind of military zone at that time, but I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but that it might be misunderstood in that way. So if you're talking about the area, we're just talking about geographical area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, you've heard this conversation. I want to ask you now the same question. During this 20th of April --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: All right. I want to substitute the word "Dukagjin area" for Dukagjin Zone." Do you still have the question in mind, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I understood your question. We discussed about the current situation of the members of the KLA at that part to which Serbian forces were attempted. There was shelling and also firing from all kinds of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Every day, there were people who were injured. It was grave situation. I saw from his face that he was very concerned about the KLA members, so we discussed about the organisation, how we could organise things better in order to protect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I understand that. And I want to ask you now about that -- that KLA organisation that was discussed at that time and that was existing. I want to ask you simply: During your April of -- your mid-April, your April 20th of 1998 visit to Irzniq, was there a KLA presence in the village of Irzniq at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: At the time, there were. The organisation in the village had just begun. After 6th of April, they had come out in public in the village, but only with a limited quantity of weapons. The organisation was still at very initial stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Can you please describe that organisation for us, please? What were the -- the posts held, or just give us some more information about that, please, if you could?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: If you're asking me about that meeting with Ramush Haradinaj, at that meeting I did not intervene, I did not ask questions about security. At the end, I promise to him that very soon I would come back and see him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you -- beyond that meeting with Mr. Haradinaj and Toger on the 20th of April, did you have contact with other KLA members in the village of Irzniq on that trip?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm informed of another translation error, and following Your Honour's guidance, it relates to page 94, line 19, and the date which there appears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cekaj, you mentioned a date after which they had come out in public in the village. Could you repeat the date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the village of Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But could you repeat the date you said after --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So they appeared on 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said "after." Did you mean to say: "After the 16th of April"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the 16th of April. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, do you have my last question in mind? Did you meet with, on that April trip into Irzniq, any of the KLA that were in the village at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: No, I didn't meet anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, you said that - this is at line 19 - that the organisation in the village had just begun at that time. Describe the organisation for us, please, that was existing at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I am talking about the day when I met. I did not know how to describe. I did not meet anyone. I returned to Peje, where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, sir, if -- you told us earlier that there was some type of organisation in the village. I just want to ask you what it was, very simply.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: It was very simple organisation, to tell the truth. It was the beginning of a public appearance that only check-points, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Was there a village commander in place at the time?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: That I could talk to you about how -- about that after I returned, so in the second half of May I learned about the command and the staff in the village of Irzniq. But on that day I knew nothing, I had no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I wonder if it would refresh your memory, Mr. Cekaj, if I referred you to your statement, the one that you made last week, that we talked about earlier. This is at -- and I wonder -- I'm going to read a sentence to you from that and I'm going to ask you if it refreshes your memory about the level of organisation in Irzniq on -- during April of 1998, and this is at paragraph 11: "When I went to the village to meet with Ramush on 16 April 1998, I learned that the Irzniq KLA HQ had already been established." That's a quote from your statement, sir. I want to ask you if that's accurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. It's not a quote from paragraph 11 of the 92 ter statement. I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's paragraph 11 of the 9th to the 11th of May statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I thought Mr. Kearney said the statement that he was referring to earlier and introduced in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I didn't mention anything about introducing it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, I'm looking at line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, he said: "The one that you made last week that we talked about earlier," and of course in -- today Mr. Kearney has drawn the attention of the witness to statements he gave earlier and then another statement on the 14th of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not complaining. I'm simply anxious to make sure we're clear which passages is that we're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's clear that it's from the -- not the 92 ter statement but the 9th to the 11th of May statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, do you want me to read that statement again or do you have it in mind still?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Please, can you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, I'd be happy to. This is -- this is from the statement you made last week, this is the longer statement that we talked about, the one made between the 9th and the 11th of May of this year, 2007. The first sentence this paragraph 11 you say: "When I went to the village to meet with Ramush on 16 April 1998, I learned that the Irzniq KLA HQ had already been established." I want to ask you, sir, first of all, if -- if that's accurate?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: As I said, it was established on 16th of April; however, I did not talk to anyone about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And how do you know, sir, it was established on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I learnt it from the members of my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Which members of your family did you talk to in that regard, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: It was my brother; I had contacts through him. Ali was his name. However, I did not meet members of the staff because I returned to Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Cekaj, thank you for that answer. I'm just asking you simply: You're referring to the staff. Did your brother tell you who was in the staff as of 16 April of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I did not talk about that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you if the following sentence refreshes your memory in this regard, this is the next sentence from the same paragraph: "The Irzniq village commander was Maxhun Cekaj and the deputy commander was Bajram Decaj. I was told at that time that there were 15 weapons in the village and that a group of villagers had gone to Albania to collect more weapons?" I'd like to ask you, first of all, if having read those two sentences refreshes your memory in this regard?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. We mentioned this. This is accurate, but -- this is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So on -- just to summarize now. On the 16th of April of 1998, there was a village commander and a deputy village commander. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. There were also other members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you know how many other members there were at that time, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: There were Shefqet Haskaj, so the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I don't need names, Mr. Cekaj. Just tell us, if you could, please, the number of KLA soldiers existing in mid-April of 1998, when you went to visit Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Sorry, are you asking me about the documents, about the thing which I mentioned about 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: No, I'm just asking you just in general. When you went -- your first trip into Irzniq when you met with Mr. Haradinaj, you mentioned already that there was a village commander and a deputy. How many soldiers were under their command at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: At that time, a part of the villagers or members of the KLA had gone to get weapons. However, there were only 15 weapons there. This is what I have already declared.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And to go with those 15 weapons, how many KLA soldiers were there at that time in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: As far as the correct number is concerned; however, on basis of what I heard about the stuff, there were 120 but they were without weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at that time, this is mid-April of 1998, was there a Serb police or military presence in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: The Serb police had already left the village of Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you know what day it was, Mr. Cekaj, that the -- the Serb police withdrew from Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: It must have been 14th or 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That's of April?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: April, that was before the meeting I had with Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, after the -- the Serbs left the police station in Irzniq, did the KLA effectively control Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: At that time, the check-points were set up on the side of the village of Prilep with some improvised positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During the -- the interview and statement process of last week, Mr. Cekaj, did you draw a map of the KLA zone of control in the Dukagjini area in the general months of April, May, and June of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: As far as I remember, about May and April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Right, but you did draw -- draw on a map during the interview process last week while you were here in The Hague. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the Trial Chamber's permission, I would like to call up 65 ter Exhibit 1336, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the registrar is invited to attribute a number to that document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be marked for identification as P318.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Is the document in the process of being loaded?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it appears to be a large document. It may take a few second to come up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's known that maps take more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if -- do the Trial Chambers want to go right to 7.00 or should we start with this tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it depends on how much time it takes. If it would take considerable time, then rather wait until it's on the screen and then perhaps put no questions or not more than one or two. I'd like to stop at two minutes to 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Perhaps while that's loading, Your Honour, I can -- I can ask a question or two at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, while we're waiting for this map to appear on the screen, when you filled in the map did you -- do you remember writing words on the top and the bottom of the map?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I wrote and indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: On the bottom of the map -- I'm sorry. On the bottom of the map, do you remember writing your own name and the date that you were drawing on the map?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: I wrote and put the signature as well as the months in which KLA was involved in that material. However, that was not for April, I think, but for other months, that is, after 15th of May, if I'm not right -- wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we now have the map on the screen. I'm going to ask the witness first --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Can you see that map, Mr. Cekaj?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, but it's very unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I wonder if we could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's very, very small.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I wonder if we could magnify this map, Your Honour, to allow the witness to see the writing on the top and the bottom if we may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if we -- after you've asked the witness that I think we should take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Can we start with the bottom, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, the words there that you see in the bottom of the exhibit, you mentioned earlier that you signed this document. Is that your signature there, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, it's my name and my surname, the date, it's exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That's the date that you drew on that map. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, please, if we can move to the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The words in Albanian there "Prill - Qershor - '98" can you explain to us if you wrote those words and what they mean in English and what you were -- first of all, tell us those two answers, please?

utterances.speaker: SHEMSEDIN CEKAJ
utterances.text: April-June, this is how it is written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I think we should --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked me where the KLA soldiers could move at that time, so this was the area in which they could move. They did not have positions at that time, only the villages were under attack so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cekaj, it's 7.00. We'll stop for the day. Mr. Kearney, I take it that this is a -- I take it that tomorrow Mr. Kearney will continue with putting questions on this map. Before we finally adjourn, I'd like to invite Mr. Usher to escort Mr. Cekaj out of the courtroom. Mr. Cekaj, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, the testimony you've given today and the testimony you're still about to give tomorrow. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you then please follow the usher. Mr. Kearney, quite simple. The witness was scheduled for two hours. Do you think you would manage?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: May I have a moment before I answer, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Coming into the courtroom, Your Honour, I had -- I had planned on taking two hours. Given some of the initial questioning, I may take a little longer than that. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let's assume that since you have had now, I think, approximately 45, 50 minutes, would another hour do?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, would another one hour and a half do? That would bring you to two hours -- two and a half hours altogether. Would that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, I hope so, sir, depending a bit on the witness himself, but yes, I'll certainly try to hit that goal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask the Defence how much time they have in mind they would need for cross-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Assuming that Mr. Kearney hits his goal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- I would aim to be between one and a half and one and three-quarters hours with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Other counsel, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 45 minutes to an hour and five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Approximately seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey, it's good that you say it's approximate and not exactly seven minutes. I have to do some calculations. Tomorrow, we have four hours in court. Let me just re-read again what the answers exactly were in order not to make any mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, may I mention one thing during the Court's calculation? This will be a map- and document-intensive witness for the Prosecution. So I know that the process of just calling up those documents takes some time itself, so there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, if you would give Mr. Registrar a list so that he well in advance in the subsequent order you would like to use these maps, that already on the administrative level it can be uploaded so that we don't lose time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The Prosecution has given an indication to the Defence as to the documents they intend to use, I'm not talking about the maps but the contemporary documents. They are all, as far as we can gather, documents that have been selected from the bundle that the Defence produced to deal with the cross-examination of Rrustem Tetaj. In other words, there is a hard copy bundle with those documents which already have an index, and they're all now marked for identification on the index, I believe, with Madam Registrar's help. So it may be, in order to keep Mr. Kearney within his time-frame, if that bundle were available tomorrow, he could -- he could use the paper copies, which will save all the calling-up time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I go back to my calculations. Yes. From what I see on the basis of the information the parties have given, it -- it would be approximately three and a half -- four and a half hours which would be needed. I would very much urge the parties -- that means, Mr. Kearney, tomorrow you have one and a half hour available. Mr. Emmerson, you're expected to finish within one hour and 35 minutes. Mr. Guy-Smith, you are expected to finish in 55 minutes. And you, Mr. Harvey, in six minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Deal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me now do the calculations again. Now, I have to deduce from all parties, in order to save the six minutes from Mr. Harvey, you would have one hour, 25 minutes, Mr. Kearney; Mr. Emmerson, 1.30; Mr. Guy-Smith, you have 50 minutes. Let's try to start in time. This is not a complaint. Sometimes when we are outside this courtroom, we are waiting for everyone to be ready in the courtroom. It happens now and then as well that people in the courtroom are waiting until we have finished our discussions out of the courtroom. So it's not blaming anyone, but let's try to get started tomorrow, and tomorrow would be quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom exactly. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.07 p.m.,
